title: The Sliding Scale
logline: Robin's childhood hockey hero tells her, between segments, that she has been saying 'athalete' on air for six years, and Ted, who once corrected a bishop, knew all along and never said a word. Robin's hunt for the reason exposes everything the gang has been quietly letting slide for each other, Barney declares the Era of Correction, and four days of total accuracy nearly end a marriage, a friendship and Barney's face.
coldOpen: Kids, I have corrected a lot of people in my life. Waiters. Tour guides. One bishop. But there was one mistake I let slide for six years, and in 2013, your Aunt Robin found out about it.

couch.line: The other bishops had heard about me.

guests.name: Gord Lacasse
guests.role: 'The Wall', a retired Canadian NHL goaltender and Robin's childhood hero; gravel-voiced, blunt and unflappable, calls everyone 'kid', and keeps an exact count of everything, because goalies count

guests.name: Simone Arceneaux
guests.role: a sommelier at the MacLaren's bar who confidently mispronounces Moët and walks out the moment Barney is finally right

scenes.summary: Robin interviews her childhood hero, goalie Gord 'The Wall' Lacasse, and calls him the greatest Canadian athalete. Off air he tells her it's two syllables, she's said it 2,114 times, and his beer league in Moose Jaw drinks to it. Patrice reveals it's the top viewer complaint, and that a man calls the tip line every time and just sighs, like a professor. He once got as far as 'Actually.' Robin: Ted.

beats.line: It started the day Aunt Robin met her childhood hero. Live on the air.
Welcome back. My next guest played fourteen seasons in net. Four hundred stitches. One nickname.
Gord The Wall Lacasse.
Four hundred and twelve stitches. I count. Goalies count.
I had your poster over my bed for nine years. The only man my father ever allowed in my room.
Gord, you're the greatest Canadian athalete of your generation. How does that feel?
Say that again.
The greatest Canadian athalete.
Huh.
We'll be right back.
Kid. It's athlete. Two syllables.
That's what I said. Athalete.
That's three.
Ath. A. Lete.
Oh my god. That's three.
You've said it on this channel two thousand one hundred and fourteen times.
How could you possibly know that?
My beer league in Moose Jaw takes a drink every time you say it. We call it the Scherbatsky.
Olympics were rough. Fella named Dougie had to be airlifted.
Patrice. Did you know about this?
Everybody knows, Robin! It's our number one viewer complaint! I made a chart!
Six years running! Sandy's ties never stood a chance.
beats.title: Viewer Complaints, 2007 to 2013

beats.line: Six years? Why didn't anybody tell me?
We put a note in the suggestion box! You set the suggestion box on fire!
It had suggestions in it.
My favorite is the man who calls the tip line every time you say it. He never says a word. He just sighs.
Long, disappointed sighs. Like a professor. Once he got as far as actually, and hung up.
Ted.

scenes.summary: Ted lectures Wendy on brusketta and proper 'pronounciation' while Marshall and Lily exchange a look; Barney orders Mo-ay and Wendy pauses. Robin storms in. Ted dodges with a compliment, the sighing city. Everyone knew. Robin outs Barney's Mo-ay, Lily produces her list of everything they let slide (Ted isn't on it, and he's thrilled), and Lily and Marshall correct each other's vows and kindergarten vocabulary. Barney declares no more sliding; Ted is ecstatic. Asked why, Ted flees to correct an appetizer.

beats.line: Wendy, it's brusketta. Hard C. The Italians would weep.
Ted, it's a tomato on toast.
And it deserves the proper pronounciation.
Ignore him, Wendy. A bottle of your finest Mo-ay. Ted's being Ted.
Coming right up.
Ted. How many syllables are in athlete?
Two?
And how many do I say?
A festive number.
Six years, Ted. You knew for six years.
Kids, I had two options. Lie to Robin Scherbatsky, or tell the truth to Robin Scherbatsky. I went with option three.
Is that a new jacket? It's very slimming.
You corrected a bishop. At a christening.
He said Byzantine wrong, Robin. In front of a baby. That baby deserved better.
And you call my tip line. To sigh.
Lots of men sigh, Robin. This is New York. It's a sighing city.
Did all of you know?
Define know.
Marshall and I held a vote in 2008. It was unanimous.
I cried. But I voted.
Don't look at me. I never correct a woman. It's tacky. Like pronouncing the T in Mo-ay.
Barney. It's Mo-wet.
It's French, Robin. The T is silent. Like a ninja.
The family was Dutch. You pronounce the T.
Ted?
She's right, buddy.
I have said Mo-ay to four hundred women!
Some of them were sommeliers!
And you let me?
Barney, it was the best part of my week.
What else? What else are you people letting slide?
Funny you should ask.
I keep a list. For emergencies.
beats.title: Things We Let Slide

beats.line: I'm not on it! Not one entry! I'm framing this.
Hold on. What's wrong with intensive purposes?
Baby. It's intents and purposes.
Since when?
Since always. You said it in your wedding vows.
For all intensive purposes, I'm yours.
My grandmother cried.
She was laughing, Marshall.
Oh yeah? Well, it's specifically. Not pacifically.
Pacifically is a word!
It's an ocean, Lily!
I've taught it to twenty-two five-year-olds.
That's it. This group is built on lies. As of tonight, nobody lets anything slide.
Every mistake, corrected on the spot. Welcome to the Era of Correction.
Yes! I have waited my entire life for someone to say that sentence.
Great. Then you go first. Why didn't you tell me?
Wendy! It's brusketta! Hard C!
He's hiding behind an appetizer.

scenes.summary: Montage of the Era of Correction: Barney finally says Moët right and loses a sommelier, Lily reads Marshall page nine of her list, Ted corrects a cabbie in bliss, Robin can't fix her word. Day five, in a cab: Barney is in urgent care, Lily corrects Marshall's sneeze. Ted coaches Robin for tomorrow's live tribute, where the word appears three times, and says 'pronounciation'; Marshall and Lily, who correct everything now, say nothing. Ted still can't say why and bails out of the cab. Lily and Marshall tell Robin the gang's biggest secret: Ted says pronounciation, and nobody has ever told him. Robin plans to tell him live; Lily is bringing the toast.

beats.line: And so began the Era of Correction. It lasted four days.
I'm a sommelier, and I would love a glass of Mo-ay.
Actually, it's Mo-wet. The family was Dutch. Where are you going?
Page nine. It's not a doggy-dog world, Marshall. It's dog eat dog.
Oh, that's so much worse.
Sir, it's How-ston Street. Not Hyoo-ston. Best week of my life.
Ath. Lete. Ath. A. Oh, come on.
By day five, the Era of Correction had a body count.
Where's Barney?
Urgent care. He corrected a bouncer's grammar. During the headlock.
Ah. Ah. Choo.
Two syllables, Marshall. Ask Robin.
She corrects my sneezes now. This morning she corrected the way I said I love you.
You said it like a question.
Everything's a question now, Lily! I don't know how to say waffles anymore!
Ted, focus. Tomorrow night they retire Gord's jersey. I read the tribute live. The word's in there three times.
Then we practice. Repeat after me. Athlete.
Ath. Lete.
Yes! Again! Faster!
Athalete.
It grows back, Ted! Like a playoff beard!
Robin, it's all about pronounciation. Tongue behind the teeth. Let the word breathe.
Why did you two just stop breathing?
Great tip.
Tongue. Teeth. Breathing. All correct. All very correct.
Ted. Real answer. Why didn't you tell me?
I can't.
Can't, or won't?
Both. It's a two-syllable situation.
Driver, I'll get out here. I'll walk. It's only forty blocks.
It's raining.
Okay. What was that? He said pronounciation and you both went pale.
Because it's pronunciation.
That's what he said. Pronounciation.
There's no noun in it. It's nun. Pro, nun, ciation.
That's insane. It's pronounce!
I know! English is a monster!
And you never told him? You correct your husband's sneezes!
Robin, some things you don't take from a man.
Also, I'm saving it. For his wedding toast. I've had the toast written since 2005.
Barney had it engraved on a watch. He's never given it to him.
So the one guy who corrects everybody is the one guy nobody corrects.
Well. Tomorrow night he finds out. Live. On my channel.
Oh, I'm bringing the toast.

scenes.summary: Before the live tribute, Ted finally explains: on the roof in 2007, a drunk Robin told him the one nice thing her father ever said was 'you're a real athalete', and made him swear never to bring it up. He wasn't going to take a syllable off it. Also, she owns five guns. Gord admits his own dad said it too, and was also wrong. The gang arrives, done with correcting: Barney corrected a woman's name to her face, and Marshall and Lily reconcile in each other's mistakes. Ted announces that good pronounciation isn't everything; Barney starts to correct him and Robin stops him cold, letting it slide. Robin goes live and says it her way. Gord: Drink. Future Ted still says pronounciation, and his kids let it slide.

beats.line: Three athletes in the script, kid. You ready?
I practiced all night. My neighbor slid a note under my door. It just said two.
Robin. Before you go on. I owe you an answer.
Two syllables, Mosby. Go.
Do you remember the roof, in 2007? Your first sports story? The bottle of scotch?
I remember the scotch.
My dad never once said he was proud of me. Not even when I won junior trap shooting.
But one time, after a hockey game, he knocked on my helmet and said, you're a real athalete, kid.
Ath—
What?
Nothing. That's a great word.
If you ever bring this up again, I will shoot you.
Fair.
You said it like it was the only trophy you ever got. I wasn't going to take a syllable off it.
You remembered that.
Also, you said you'd shoot me. You own four guns.
Five.
And the sighing?
It had to go somewhere, Robin. A man can only hold in so many syllables.
For what it's worth, kid, my old man said athalete too.
Really?
Yep. He was also wrong.
I'm calling it. The Era of Correction is over. Last night I corrected a woman's name. To her face.
Turns out she knew.
Lilypad, I miss it. I miss pacifically. I want my wife back. Ocean and all.
Marshmallow. For all intensive purposes, you've got her.
Okay. Robin. We're ready for the main event.
Guys, I learned something this week. Good pronounciation isn't everything.
Actually, Ted, it's pro—
Barney!
It's pro what?
Profound. He said profound. What you just said was profound.
My toast!
My watch!
Save them for his wedding.
Why is everybody looking at me like that?
No reason, buddy. You just look really profound.
Live in five. Four. I count.
Good evening. Tonight we honor a Canadian legend.
And one heck of an athalete.
Drink.
Aunt Robin said athalete on the air for nine more years. And I learned the real secret of good pronounciation: sometimes you let it slide.
Should we tell him?
Nah. We love him.
Tell me what?
